system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: The Context Layer services dynamically assemble prompts using data from both the message pool and memory bank
system_prompt_style.note: Paper-only architecture description; no code available.

env_context_strategy.note: Paper only; no repository or config surface to inspect.

context_compaction.note: Paper only; no history-processing code or config available.

observation_format.note: Paper mentions JSON payloads to resources but not how observations are shown to the model.

tool_call_format.note: Resources are wrapped as REST APIs; the model-side call syntax is not described.

tool_count.note: Tools are retrieved dynamically from Gateway Agents; no default tool count is given.

edit_primitive.note: No edit tool is described; paper only.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: A successfully registered resource will be accompanied with crucial details, such as the resource's name, application programming interface (API), input and output schema, and API documentation.
tool_schema_source.note: Resource schemas and manifests are authored by the registering developers.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: DAWN uses an open protocol to interact and communicate between distributed components.
protocol_standardization.note: The paper describes an unnamed open protocol over REST/HTTPS. MCP, A2A and ACP are cited as related work, not as protocols DAWN speaks.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: The Principal Agent's planner uses ReAct [29], as the default reasoning strategy
loop_primitives.note: ReAct is the stated default. Plan-then-execute via a task graph (FSM) is also described, and ReWOO/ToT are mentioned as alternatives developers may adopt.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: Internally, the task graph created from the each task list is implemented as a finite state machine whose nodes are agents or agent ensembles.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: The Principal Agent acts as an autonomous planner-composer and central orchestrator within the DAWN framework.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: delegating subtasks' execution to the corresponding resources
delegation_mechanism.note: Delegation is by calling remote agent resources through REST references; this is the closest allowed value.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: It then compiles an execution graph showing each subtask and corresponding resource, local or remote, which the user can approve.
human_in_loop.note: Operating mode (No-LLM, Copilot, LLM Agent) is selectable. The HR example also waits for a human after each agentic step.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: the Orchestration Layer maintains the global state, tracking the progress of task execution across all nodes in the workflow
short_term_state.note: A scratchpad is also described in the Context Layer.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: a memory bank to store long-term data and user preferences, supporting long context, in-session, cross-session, multi-turn conversations
long_term_memory.note: The storage mechanism is unspecified; episodic_db is the closest value.

state_persistence.note: The paper claims the design is 'easier to trace and restart', but no resume mechanism is shown.

self_verification.note: LLM-as-a-judge is mentioned only generically and for the paper's evaluation, not as a harness mechanism.

retry_policy.note: Paper only; the task-level retry policy is not specified.

rollback.note: Paper only; no place where rollback would be declared was available.

termination_condition.note: The paper says the process repeats until the request is addressed, but gives no explicit termination mechanism.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: along with caching (references to) resources retrieved from Gateway Agents using a Least Recently Used (LRU) strategy
cost_controls.note: This caches resource references, not prompts; it is the closest allowed value.

timeouts.note: Paper only; no timeout configuration is described.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: when the Principal Agents executes resources from a Gateway Agent, it is in reality making an API call to the resource
execution_isolation.note: The paper also mentions a built-in run-time environment for the Principal Agent.

filesystem_access.note: Paper only; filesystem access is not described.

network_policy.note: Paper only; HTTPS channels are described, but no egress policy.

permission_model.evidence_quote: guardrails through algorithms designed to filter inputs and outputs
permission_model.note: The SSC layer screens actions; the mechanism is not specified.

tracing.note: Telemetry is mentioned, but its format is unspecified.

replayability.note: Paper only; no replay facility is described or ruled out.

eval_hooks.note: No repository was available to check for a built-in evaluation runner.

guardrails.evidence_quote: The Principal Agent and each of the Gateway Agents implement safety, security, and compliance screening to scrub agentic resources' inputs and outputs.

target_domain.evidence_quote: allows globally distributed agents of any provenance to be registered, discovered, and organized for building AI-based applications and solutions

open_source.note: No repository or licence is given in the evidence.

model_agnostic.note: GPT-4o is used in the demonstration; no LLM client abstraction is described.

primary_artifact.note: No repository URL is given in the evidence.

first_release_date.note: No release tag and no paper v1 date appear in the evidence; only the v3 date is shown.

pinned_version.note: No repository is available; the paper version is arXiv 2410.22339v3.
